title: Urgent warning about 'an epidemic' of patients as young as three with horrible burns for exploiting e-scooters
text:
Surgeons have warned that they are seeing ‘an epidemic’ of patients, some as young as three, with horrible burns and that change the lives caused by overheated and exploited batteries of electronic bicycles and electronic scooters.
The devices, which have powerful electric motors, have become common, with pedestrians under the threat of cyclists that accelerate through parks and pavements. However, doctors have also blamed vehicles for a strong increase in Burns’s victims.
Surgeons who treat these injuries often change their lives are asking for danger labels to increase public awareness, while cases will increase as the number of electronic bicycles and scooters in the United Kingdom, currently around 550,000, continue increasing.
They also revealed that more people, especially young children, are receiving burns of playing batteries while loading.
Adam Kerman, 44, from Leinsestershire, almost died of an explosion of the battery in 2023. While carrying his e-Scooter, Tres’s father heard an explosion. When he went to a check, he was flown back by a flame ball.
When his floor caught fire, he escaped, but his airway was very burned and suffered burns in 11 percent of his body.
Last night he said: ‘It was not mentioned that this could happen. Permanent warning labels are needed to make sure that no one else has to go through the nightmare that I have passed.
The British Association of Plastic, Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgeons (Bapras) is also asking for action. Its president, the plastic surgeon Mani Ragbir, said: “Manufacturers, vendors and markets must assume responsibility, including compensation of these hazards.”
The London Fire Brigade published images of an Explosion of Scooter E batteries in an attempt to urge users to load their vehicles safely
The residents in the shared house in Harlesden, northwest of London, had to be relocated due to the devastation of the fire
The devices, which have powerful electric motors, have become common, with pedestrians under the threat of cyclists that accelerate through parks and pavements
The research presented to Bapras by the Faculty of Medicine of the University of Manchester has reviewed evidence on patients worldwide injured by batteries in personal mobility devices (PMD), the term for electronic bicycles and scooters.
PMDs use lithium -ion batteries, which are cheaper to do and more powerful than older types of rechargeable batteries, but contain flammable chemicals.
John Warner-Levy, main author of the study, said: ‘If they remain in charge for too long, or the incorrect charger is used, they can overheat, causing an internal short circuit. More and more heat is generated along with increasing amounts of combustible gases such as hydrogen and carbon monoxide. At a certain point, detonate in a large fireball.
Although data on Burns’s victims are collected throughout the United Kingdom, the cause is not always on the list, which means that there is no definitive evidence on the number of battery burns. However, the London Fire Brigade said that 143 fires were caused by electronic bicycles and 36 by E-Scooters in London in 2023, causing three deaths and 60 injuries.
Warner-Levy added: ‘With the PMDs that become even more popular in Britain, there is likely that there is a corresponding increase in burns.
“In Singapore and China, which are in years in terms of adoption of PMD, there are many more reports of injury of this type of explosions.”
Private property scooters are illegal to travel on public roads and bicycle routes. Electronic bicycles are legal if the engine only helps a pedaling pilot and is limited to 15.5 mph. But the subsequent DIY kits are available for both.
Warner-Levy warned that DIY adaptations were an important source of explosions, since users ended with non-coincident components.
Damage to a property caused by an e-Scooter, in West Hampstead, northwest of London earlier this week
Photos posted by the London Fire Brigade Show Marks Chamuscadas extended on the outside of the red brick house in West Hampstead
Eight fire trucks and around 60 firefighters ran to the scene in West Hampstead, where the fire had spread along the ground floor and stairs
Another fire occurred around hours later at 2.35 in the morning on Tuesday when an electronic bicycle caught in Feltham, West London
Zeeshan Sheikh, Consultant Surgeon of the NHS Foundation of the University of Manchester, said some of the signs that a battery was becoming dangerous.
He said: ‘People should be careful with a lump in the battery housing, a peculiar smell, smoke or even a reduction in performance: these are signs of danger.
‘Never leave them (loading) unattended or chargals during the night. Follow the manufacturer guidelines and use only the recommended loaders.
The other danger of PMD batteries is when children touch the charger terminals, particularly for children. In a second fraction, its temperature can increase above 400 ° C, causing burns.
Bapras is asking for bright colors warning labels in batteries and QR codes that link fire safety advice, as well as a prohibition of DIY conversion kits.
